one_liner: Coordinate and likely lead campus housing tours for prospective students and families at George Mason University's Housing & Residence Life office in Fairfax.
fit_summary: Daniel's ease with the public suits a tours role, and Fairfax is a reasonable commute from Manassas. The job sits in university housing and student services, so it uses little of his emergency management, logistics or public health background; confirm the duties before investing time.
eligibility: No duties, qualifications or 'who may apply' details are posted; open the jobs.virginia.gov listing to confirm minimum qualifications.
Check whether the role is classified staff, wage (hourly/part-time) or a student position; tours roles are sometimes part-time or student-filled.
Check for any degree or prior higher-education/housing experience requirement, which the posting does not state.
Note any background check or evening/weekend availability requirement listed in the full posting.
strategy: Before applying, read the full posting at the URL. Look for salary, hours, classification and closing date, since none appear here. Apply early because 'open until filled' postings can close without notice.

Frame your IEM work around public-facing and coordination tasks you actually did, such as client meetings, stakeholder outreach, scheduling, or presenting to government audiences. Use your real title and duties.
Lead with your people skills, including building relationships quickly, speaking to groups, and explaining complex information clearly to the public.
Virginia state applications often include screening questions; answer honestly, and make sure your resume supports each 'yes.'
Write a short cover letter that explains why you want to join a public university. Present it as a step into Commonwealth employment and service to students and families.
Treat this as a foothold, not a destination. Keep applying to policy, legislative and emergency-management roles that use more of your background.
